title: `sum`/`avg` of a double constant
description: DuckDB's sums of doubles are IEEE (native): `inf`, `-inf`, `nan`.

Order class: a constant argument reaches `sum` and `avg` as a constant vector, and DuckDB adds it as one product per vector (`input * count`, at most 2048 rows), so `sum(0.1)` over 10 rows is 1.0 and `avg(0.1)` 0.1, where adding the ten values in turn gives 0.9999999999999999 and 0.09999999999999999. The product's error is at most u·k|x|, inside the sequential bound γ_{n−1} Σ|x_i| (Higham §4.2) and #85's. Lean's `floatSum` adds the constant n times, so this path refines neither SEQUENTIAL nor, until a lemma puts fl(k·x) among the tree sums of k copies, ANY (duckdb-sum-double).
reference: Lean: `SUM(CAST('inf' AS DOUBLE))` evaluated to a 500-digit integer, and `avg(42) OVER ()` to `inf`. The aggregate took a constant argument for an integer and added float codes; over a double column it was right. A deviation and a soundness bug. Fixed (#205): a constant argument has its declared type, so `sum(fp64)` adds doubles.

provenance.notes: Aggregate constants have their declared type.

evidence.note: Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed., SIAM 2002), ch. 4 Summation: §4.2 recursive, pairwise and any-order bounds; §4.3 compensated summation

evidence.sql: SET threads = 1; SELECT sum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, avg(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, fsum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR FROM range(10); CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v FROM range(10); SELECT sum(v)::VARCHAR, fsum(v)::VARCHAR FROM t; SELECT sum(v ORDER BY i)::VARCHAR FROM (SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v, i FROM range(10) r(i))
evidence.observed: constant argument: sum 1.0, avg 0.1, fsum 1.0; table column: sum 0.9999999999999999, fsum 1.0; sum(v ORDER BY i) 0.9999999999999999. 0.1 * 10 is 1.0 in double, the ten additions in turn 0.9999999999999999

provenance.notes: DuckDB 2.0.0 (Python, macOS arm64), a scratch script at threads = 1.
